title: Edit your seat loses its unsaved draft (and its tab) on any background redraw: governor is not a held view
detail: #/governor/edit keeps its draft (showcase, background, title, sigil) in a closure inside the view function (js/modules/governor-ui.js:660-686). The kos-redraw-1 stopgap holds background redraws only for TASK_VIEWS (js/core/ui.js:357-358), which does not list governor (nor achievements, money, goals, routines). So a soft background redraw (routines autoSync after a session or on the review ticker, js/core/routines.js:699; the Daily Review closing, js/modules/dayreview.js:92/103/661/709; the Google read-only copy loading, js/core/ext.js:364; own art loading at boot, js/main.js:307) remounts the page at once, and a cloud pull (hard) does so 45 s after the last touch. Repro on slot 20: open Edit your seat, Background tab, pick another background (Save lights up, data-state=lit), call KOS.rerender({background:'soft'}): the tab is back on Showcase, the picked background is gone and Save is no longer lit; nothing was saved. The page has a Discard/Save pair, so the user believes the draft is held until they press one.
evidence: eval on slot 20 (seeded): before {tabSel:'Background', mid pressed '1000…', lit:'lit'} → after soft rerender {afterTab:'Showcase', lit2:null}; shots/architecture-perf/gov-edit-mac.png; js/core/ui.js:357-372 (TASK_VIEWS, holdBackground); js/modules/governor-ui.js:660-686
fix: Short term: add governor (the edit arg) and any page with an in-page draft to the held list, or let a view declare itself held (e.g. KOS.views.x.holdsDraft = arg => …) so the list is not a central guess. Proper fix: the view lifecycle in the backlog (a view can veto or persist its draft before a redraw); the Edit seat draft could also live in state.ui like other per-device drafts.
rootCause: The redraw stopgap's hold list is a hand-maintained set of view ids in ui.js; any page added later with transient in-page state is unprotected by default.

title: The smoke gate is not reliable under load: five suites fail when run three at a time and pass alone
detail: Running all 113 suites with three in parallel on the shared test machine (load ~10) failed smoke2, smoke4 (vault cards not rendered in jsdom), smoke16 (wishlist cover), smoke17 (applyCosmetics not called after a pull) and smoke45 (toast announcements). Each passed when re-run alone (2-16 s). The failures are timing assumptions (fixed waits in the tests) rather than product bugs, but they make a parallel runner — the obvious answer to the gate's 20-minute CPU cost — unusable, and they would read as regressions on a slow CI machine. The gate itself is now 1,227 CPU-seconds (450 s wall with three workers); smoke56 (242 s) and smoke75 (236 s) are 39% of it.
evidence: arch20/gate-summary.txt (exit code, ms, suite; sorted by time); scratchpad logs: smoke4 'STEP anime vault renders + lazy fallback…: Error: no cards rendered' tools/smoke4.test.js:390; smoke17 'applyCosmetics was not called after a remote state applied'; smoke16 TypeError tools/smoke16.test.js:550; serial re-runs all exit 0
fix: Replace fixed sleeps in those five suites with waits on a condition (poll for the cards, the announcement, the applyCosmetics call); then add a parallel runner (npm test) with a per-suite timeout.
rootCause: Tests wait fixed times for async work (IndexedDB, timers) inside jsdom.

title: Badge measuring runs synchronously on the main thread: the Governor's Seat measures all 254 badges twice per render, and every topic tick re-measures 44 study badges
detail: KOS.achievements.list() builds a fresh context (makeCtx, js/core/achievements.js:239) and runs every badge's measure (measureOne, :296) each time it is called; nothing is memoised across calls or renders. The Governor's Seat status page calls it twice per render (js/modules/governor-ui.js:358 the arc of medals and :527 the area cards) and Edit your seat once more (:732); the Wall calls it on each tab (js/modules/achievements.js:126, 613, 747). Many measures are themselves the expensive derived reads the earlier audit found un-memoised — KOS.exams.readiness for every upcoming exam (achcatalogue.js:251-256, the 'Ready' badge), Code/Creatives/Mind evidence over every lesson, topic bands over every leaf for the ~30 unit badges (reg.unit, achcatalogue.js ~246). Owner events re-measure by domain (touch, 400 ms debounce), and the 'study' domain holds 44 badges, so every store.setCheck/setStatus (js/core/store.js:452/466 → onProgress) costs one main-thread long task some 400 ms after the tick. Measured on the dense account (machine shared, load 5-9, so absolute figures are inflated): a single onProgress('cs') produced one 541 ms long task; evaluate(['study']) took 1.3-13.5 s across runs; KOS.achievements.list() 2.4-3.9 s cold, 138 ms warm; KOS.show('governor') 0.7-22 s (3.1 s typical first render), with measureOne, reg.unit, readiness, code/creatives/mind evidence, code.stats and srs.dueCards at the top of its CPU profile.
evidence: arch20/prof-governor.txt (CPU profile of KOS.show('governor')); eval on slot 20: {listCallsPerGovernorRender:2, list first 3929 ms / second 138 ms, evalStudy 13555 then 3112 then 1324 ms}, longtask observer after KOS.achievements.onProgress('cs') = [541]; js/core/achievements.js:239-262, 296-341, 446-466; js/modules/governor-ui.js:358, 527, 732
fix: Keep the last evaluate's per-badge values (in memory, keyed by a store revision or the ledgerKey already computed at achievements.js:134) and let list() read them instead of re-measuring; measure only when the owning domain's revision moved. Run the domain re-measure in idle slices (requestIdleCallback, a few badges per slice) so a tick never blocks input. The memo layer for readiness/code evidence recommended in the backlog would cut the rest.
rootCause: list() and evaluate() both measure from scratch with a per-call context; measures reuse un-memoised derived reads; all of it runs synchronously.
